episodes.187583: A slow-moving storm system brought several inches of rainfall to most of Central Alabama from early morning on February 11 through the evening of February 12. While most areas saw at least 1-2 inches of rain, parts of southern and southeastern Central Alabama recorded as much as 8 inches, especially across parts of Lee, Macon, and Russell counties. Waves of heavy rainfall resulted in flooding along the Interstate 85 corridor during the afternoon of February 11 and again during the early morning of February 12. More storms formed in western and central parts of the area around midday February 12, ahead of an approaching cold front. A few of these storms produced hail up to penny to quarter size, notably around Tuscaloosa and Hoover, along with sporadic tree damage. After the frontal passage, flooding of large streams and creeks in Russell and Macon counties continued into February 13.
episodes.187978: A broken line of thunderstorms ahead of a cold front over the eastern Gulf of Mexico extending south from an area of low pressure moving across the southeast U.S. and Mid-Atlantic produced gusty marine winds over the Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.188078: Precipitation spread northwest into the area on the afternoon and evening of February 12th due to an approaching low-pressure system. The bulk of precipitation fell across western and central West Virginia as the system moved overhead, with most locations receiving between one and two inches of rain during the night. ||Flooding developed around midnight, with multiple reports of high water spanning Cabell, Kanawha, Lincoln, Putnam, and Clay Counties.  In Lincoln County, the Hamlin and Griffithsville river gauges exceeded bankfull levels and caused flooding in nearby fields and roadways. One fatality occurred in Roane County when a creek in Spencer exceeded its banks and flooded a nearby baseball field. Three to four feet of water filled the dugout and claimed the life of a man who had fallen asleep inside.||Lowering temperatures accompanied the departure of the system early on the 13th, allowing rain to transition to snow before precipitation exited to the east later that morning. One to three inches of snow accumulated within the higher terrain of Nicholas and Webster Counties, while a four inch observation was reported near Snowshoe in Pocahontas County.  Amounts diminished to less than an inch outside of the northeast mountains. Strong bursts of wind were also observed during this time. There was one instance of a downed tree near the town of Anstead in Fayette County.||After precipitation ceased on the 13th, high waters slowly receded over the course of the day, though a few pockets of flooding persisted in Cabell County until early on the 14th.
episodes.188684: A low pressure system brought a squall of strong to severe thunderstorms across East Tennessee, with ambient non-thunderstorm winds near or at high wind criteria. After the low passed, wrap around snow producing light accumulations occurred across higher elevations of the East TN Mountains.
episodes.188686: A low pressure system brought first a squall of strong to severe thunderstorms through Southwest Virginia, then on the backside a light snow to higher elevations.
episodes.189204: A period of persistent thunderstorms moved through the area with an initial warm front early in the morning and later a weak cold front overnight. Weak instability resulted in mostly benign activity, aside from a single report of each hail and wind damage. Rainfall amounts of 2.5 to 5 inches stretched across central Georgia, with highest amounts along the Georgia-Alabama line, between LaGrange and Columbus. Isolated flash flooding resulted from the heavy rainfall amounts.
episodes.189352: A frontal system intensified as it moved from the southern Mississippi River Valley into the Carolinas and southwestern Virginia on February 12. Some marginal instability developed ahead of the approaching low pressure that allowed for isolated severe thunderstorms to develop. These storms produced winds that knocked down trees, damaged outbuildings and a vehicle. There were also sporadic power power outages.
episodes.189353: A frontal system intensified as it moved from the southern Mississippi River Valley into the Carolinas and southeast West Virginia on February 12. Some marginal instability developed ahead of the approaching low pressure that allowed for isolated severe thunderstorms to develop. These storms produced winds that knocked a couple of trees.

events.narrative: ASOS site KPIE St. Petersburg-Clearwater International Airport reported a 48 mph wind gust.
At least one tree and two power poles were downed near the intersection of Davan Lane  and H.D. Atha Rd.

A few trees were blown down by severe thunderstorm wind gusts between Tusculum and Mosheim. Additionally, multiple strong wind gusts were recorded during the storms' passage, including 46 mph in Madisonville, 55 mph at Knoxville McGhee Tyson Airport, 56 mph at Sevierville - Pigeon Forge Airport, 40 mph at Greenville AWOS, and 52 mph in Leesburg.
A few trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds, with one falling onto a power line, on East Main Street near the Holston River.
One tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds onto a power line on Red Stone Road.

Numerous trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds in a swath from Richlands, VA to four miles ENE of Tiptop, VA. Several fell onto power lines causing scattered power outages. One tree fell onto a house as well.
One tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds blocking a lane of Scratch Gravel Road.
Multiple reports of trees blown down by powerful thunderstorm wind gusts across the county. Additionally, a 48 mph thunderstorm wind gust was recorded in Coeburn.
One tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds along B. F. Buchanan Highway.
A 40 foot shed was blown onto its side by thunderstorm winds.
A tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds blocking Red Oak Ridge. A second tree fell onto a fire truck while clearing the first tree, causing damage to the fire truck.
A tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds onto a house.
One tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds onto the Interstate 77 North off-ramp, at Virginia mile marker 41.
High water was observed at the Kanawha Boulevard West Dupont Avenue underpass near the Chemours Plant in Belle.
Flooding was observed on Four Mile Creek Road in the city of Branchland. A water rescue was conducted during the flooding.

Tanner Run flooded the Spencer Middle School baseball field. A fatality occurred when a man fell asleep in the dugout and was swept away. Local responders found him later that afternoon after the flood waters had receded.
High water was observed on Quick Road at Ozzie Lane near the town of Quick.
High water was observed on Lens Creek Road at Left Fork Road near Hernshaw.
In Malden, high water was observed on Dry Branch Road at Fleck Drive.
High water was observed in Midland Avenue at Hastings Drive in Belle.
Numerous roadways across the county remained impassable the day after up to eight inches of rain fell in northern Russell County, mainly along flooded creeks and streams.

Montgomery Fire/Rescue performed evacuations of homes surrounded by floodwater along Harmony St and Dumas St. A portion of Hayneville Rd was inaccessible by vehicle. Nearby Catoma Creek crested in moderate flood stage at 26.1 ft around 6 AM CST.
A large barn and a few smaller sheds were blown down by thunderstorm winds.
High water was observed at the intersection of Falcon Drive and Sugar Creek Drive in Charleston.

The Mud River gauge near Griffithsville exceeded a bankfull level of 12 feet shortly after midnight on the 13th of February. The river crested around 13.4 feet, then lowered below bankfull later that morning. While the river was out of its banks, fields and low areas along the Middle Fork of the Mud River in the vicinity of the gauge flooded.
High water was observed between Slaughters Creek Road and Little Creek Road.
High water was observed on North Poplar Fork Road and Summerbrook Lane.

Macon County EMA informed local media about a person requiring a water rescue from a submerged vehicle that entered floodwaters of Uphapee Creek after the driver moved and drove around barricades on Wire Road/Macon County Road 53 at approximately 2:00 AM CST. A river gauge just downstream indicated the creek crested at 27.6 ft around this time.
High water was observed around the 4700 block of Witcher Creek Road.
In the town of Belle, high water was observed on Simmons Creek Road near Simmons Creek Church.
High water was observed in the 2700 block of Third Avenue in East Bank.
High water was observed around the 11000 block of MacCorkle Avenue SE in Marmet.
High water was observed between Paint Creek and MacCorkle Avenue SE in Hansford.
Flooding was observed at the 7400 block of US 60 outside of Hurricane.

The Mud River gauge at Hamlin exceeded a bankfull level of 13 feet on the morning of February 13th. After rising to a crest around 13.3 feet late that morning, the river gradually lowered and returned to its banks in the afternoon. Sections of Route 3 in West Hamlin flooded as a result.
Simons Fork exceeded its banks and caused flooding on Simons Fork Road.
Route 61 in Handley was closed due to high water for a period of time.
Flooding from Trace Fork occurred along portions of Clymers Creek Road and Turkey Creek Road.
